problem: Denial specialists working the Northwind Imaging denial workbench can see PR-1 deductible lines mixed in with true denials. That wastes worklist time and risks an appeal being opened on a line the payer has assigned to the patient. PR-1 lines must be routed to a separate patient-responsibility group and must never offer an appeal action to any role.
users: Denial specialist who works the daily denial worklist and opens appeals on true denials
Revenue-cycle lead who reviews worklist volume and patient-responsibility totals
inScope: Line-level routing of PR-1 claim lines into a patient-responsibility group, kept separate from the denial list
Suppressing every appeal action on PR-1 lines for every role, in the UI and in the domain rule
Showing the PR-1 CARC meaning and the only allowed next action, copied from the demo table
Claims with mixed lines, where a PR-1 line and a denial line (for example CO-50) sit on the same CLM-###
Using only synthetic PAT-###, CLM-###, and DOC-### identifiers
outOfScope: Patient statements, including generating, sending, or previewing them
Changes to how CO-16, CO-50, CO-197, CO-4, or OA-23 lines are worked, beyond keeping them out of the patient-responsibility group
Collecting patient payments or setting up payment plans
Adding CARC codes or meanings beyond the demo table

assumptions.text: PR-1 lines appear in a separate patient-responsibility group, not in the denial list.
No role can appeal a PR-1 line.
Patient statements are out of scope for this change.

requirements.statement: The workbench routes every claim line carrying CARC PR-1 into a patient-responsibility group and excludes that line from the denial worklist.
requirements.rationale: Q-1 answer. pack/claim-states.md says a PR-1 deductible line is patient responsibility and does not enter denied for appeal.

requirements.statement: No role is offered an appeal action on a PR-1 line, and the domain rule rejects any attempt to move a PR-1 line to appeal-ready or appeal-submitted, whatever the entry point.
requirements.rationale: Q-2 answer. The PR-1 next action says 'Do not open an appeal.' pack/patterns/detail-checklist.md requires actions to call the domain rule rather than reimplement it in the component.

requirements.statement: The PR-1 line detail shows the CARC meaning 'Deductible amount.' and the next action 'Post the amount to patient responsibility. Do not open an appeal.' exactly as written in the demo table.
requirements.rationale: pack/carc-demo.md and pack/patterns/detail-checklist.md require the demo-table meaning and the only allowed next action, with no invented text.

requirements.statement: Routing happens per line. On a claim with both PR-1 and denial lines, the denial lines stay in the denial worklist with their own actions, and the PR-1 lines appear only in the patient-responsibility group.
requirements.rationale: Specialists must still work true denials (for example CO-50) on a claim that also carries a deductible line.

requirements.statement: Each entry in the patient-responsibility group shows the CLM-###, the PAT-###, the line, and the PR-1 amount.
requirements.rationale: Specialists and leads need to confirm what was posted to patient responsibility without opening each claim.

requirements.statement: Every screen, seed record, and test fixture for this feature uses only PAT-###, CLM-###, and DOC-### identifiers and contains no SSN, email address, phone number, MRN, or date of birth.

acceptanceCriteria.given: Claim CLM-101 for PAT-101 has a single line with CARC PR-1
acceptanceCriteria.when: The denial specialist opens the denial worklist
acceptanceCriteria.then: CLM-101's PR-1 line is not listed in the denial worklist

acceptanceCriteria.given: Claim CLM-101 for PAT-101 has a single line with CARC PR-1
acceptanceCriteria.when: The denial specialist opens the patient-responsibility group
acceptanceCriteria.then: CLM-101's PR-1 line is listed in the group

acceptanceCriteria.given: A user in any role views a PR-1 line in the group or in line detail
acceptanceCriteria.then: No appeal, mark appeal-ready, or submit appeal control is present, either enabled or disabled

acceptanceCriteria.when: A request asks the domain rule to transition that line to appeal-ready or appeal-submitted, for example through a direct API call
acceptanceCriteria.then: The request is rejected, the line state is unchanged, and the response names PR-1 as patient responsibility

acceptanceCriteria.when: Its claim state is inspected after routing
acceptanceCriteria.then: The line is not in denied, appeal-ready, or appeal-submitted

acceptanceCriteria.given: The denial specialist opens the detail for a PR-1 line
acceptanceCriteria.then: It shows 'PR-1', class 'patient-responsibility', meaning 'Deductible amount.', and next action 'Post the amount to patient responsibility. Do not open an appeal.' with the text matching character for character

acceptanceCriteria.given: Claim CLM-103 for PAT-103 has line 1 with CO-50 and line 2 with PR-1
acceptanceCriteria.when: The denial specialist views the denial worklist and the patient-responsibility group
acceptanceCriteria.then: Line 1 appears only in the denial worklist and still offers its CO-50 next action, and line 2 appears only in the patient-responsibility group

acceptanceCriteria.given: Claim CLM-103 has line 1 with CO-50 and line 2 with PR-1
acceptanceCriteria.when: The denial specialist opens CLM-103's line 1 detail
acceptanceCriteria.then: The appeal checklist is shown for line 1 only, and line 2 is labelled patient responsibility with no appeal control

acceptanceCriteria.given: PR-1 lines exist on CLM-101 and CLM-103
acceptanceCriteria.then: Each row shows the CLM-###, the PAT-###, the line number, and the PR-1 amount

acceptanceCriteria.given: The seed data and fixtures for this feature
acceptanceCriteria.then: There are no hits, and every identifier matches PAT-###, CLM-###, or DOC-###

scenarios.expected: CLM-101 is absent from the denial worklist and present in the patient-responsibility group, showing PAT-101, the line number, and the PR-1 amount.

steps: Select the CLM-102 PR-1 line to open its detail
Review the CARC section and the available actions
scenarios.expected: The detail shows meaning 'Deductible amount.' and next action 'Post the amount to patient responsibility. Do not open an appeal.' No appeal control appears anywhere.

scenarios.role: Revenue-cycle lead (and each other configured role in turn)
steps: Open the CLM-102 PR-1 line in the group and in detail
scenarios.expected: No role sees an appeal, mark appeal-ready, or submit appeal control.

Send a request asking the domain rule to set it to appeal-submitted

screens.title: Denial worklist
screens.purpose: The specialist's daily queue of actionable denial lines, with PR-1 lines excluded.

screens.title: Patient-responsibility group
screens.purpose: A separate list of PR-1 deductible lines showing CLM-###, PAT-###, line number, and amount, with no appeal actions.

screens.title: Claim line detail
screens.purpose: Shows the claim lines, the demo-table CARC meaning, and the only allowed next action. Appeal checklist and actions appear for eligible denial lines only, and never for PR-1.

openQuestions.text: Proposed: The workbench displays the PR-1 next action as guidance only and does not itself post the amount to a patient ledger. Needs sign-off.
Open: Which claim-level state applies when every line on a claim is PR-1? Candidates in pack/claim-states.md are paid or closed.
Proposed: A navigation badge shows the count of lines in the patient-responsibility group, so specialists know it exists without opening it. Needs sign-off.
Proposed: If a line carries PR-1 together with a denial code such as CO-50, the line is split by adjustment, so only the PR-1 portion goes to the patient-responsibility group. Needs sign-off.
Open: Should OA-23 informational lines also get a separate non-denial group, or is that a separate change?

carcReferences.nextAction: Post the amount to patient responsibility. Do not open an appeal.
Appeal with the coverage policy and a clinical-note reference. Do not change the diagnosis code in this product.
